title: Applied ML Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:

This playbook standardizes how Applied ML and Evals responds to model quality regressions detected by the eval harness, production monitoring, or customer reports. It covers initial detection, automated triage steps, human escalation, and postmortem actions across the following subdomains: eval harness alerts, prompt set regressions, quantization-induced quality drops, and onboarding regressions for new model variants.

Purpose and scope:
- Ensure consistent, fast, and auditable response to regressions that affect customer-facing outputs or internal benchmarks.
- Applicable to Redwood Inference hosted models, dedicated pools, and private deployments (where customer permissions allow).
- Excludes low-severity cosmetic language changes that do not change correctness or safety classifications (see Severity definitions).

Severity definitions (applies to eval alerts and production regressions):
1) Sev-1 (Critical): Large-scale regression (>5% drop) on core prompt sets or safety/evasiveness metrics impacting >90th percentile customers, or regressions causing safety violations.
2) Sev-2 (High): Noticeable quality drop (1-5% delta) on important prompt sets, or customer-visible degradation for paid customers.
3) Sev-3 (Medium): Small regressions on non-critical prompt sets, or noisy/ambiguous eval fluctuations.
4) Sev-4 (Low): Informational anomalies, single-run noise, or expected variability during model rollouts.

Ownership and roles:
- Reporter: the alerting system or engineer who filed the ticket.
- Triage Lead: Applied ML on-call engineer (rotating).
- Model Owner: the team that owns the model in the model catalog (e.g., model-onboarding or model-hosting).
- Release Engineer: eng-serving-runtime owner for kernel/scheduling regressions.
- Customer Success: notified for customer-impact regressions.

Alert sources and first actions:
- Eval harness automated alerts (priority): run automated triage job (eval-triage-run) that collects latest runs, prompt-set diffs, token-level degradations, and quantization profile changes.
- Production monitoring (observability console): collect sample requests, model version, routing policy, and latency/cost metadata.
- Customer support / security: attach transcript, model id, and tenant routing info.

Automated triage checklist (run within 15 minutes of alert):
1) Retrieve failing eval harness run: eval-triage-run --run-id <id> --output /tmp/triage-<id>.json
2) Compute delta against the baseline (default baseline: last-production-stable tagged run).
3) Classify failure: prompt-set coverage, hallucination/regressions, safety false-positive/neg, latency-induced truncation, or quantization accuracy drop.
4) If quantization suspected, run quantization-diff with profiles: quant-diff --orig-profile fp16 --new-profile int8 --samples /tmp/triage-<id>.json
5) Attach artifacts to ticket: failing prompts, model logs, KV-cache lookup traces, and token probability deltas.

Quick decision matrix (Triage Lead):
- If delta >5% on core prompt sets or safety metrics => declare Sev-1 and initiate cross-team incident.
- If delta between 1-5% on critical prompts => Sev-2, add to next model rollback window or canary rollback.
- If quantization delta > acceptable threshold (default 0.8% exact-match drop for high-precision tasks) => mark as quantization regression and flag for quant-profile rollback.
- If regression appears only under heavy batching/latency conditions => route to eng-serving-runtime kernel-and-scheduling.

Investigation playbook (human steps):
1) Reproduce locally using eval-harness: clone harness, checkout run commit, run: make reproduce RUN_ID=<id> ENV=controlled --prompt-set <set> --model <model-id>.
2) Check model artifact differences: model checksum, tokenizer changes, generation config (temperature, top_p), and soft-prompt embeddings.
3) Inspect quantization profile changes and recent quantization jobs: list quant jobs via qa/quant-jobs --since 30d --model <model-id>.
4) Check rollout and routing policy history: api: GET /model-routing/<model-id>/history?since=48h
5) Validate against golden prompt-set: rerun failing prompts on baseline + previous two model versions to confirm regression start-point.

Common root causes and remediation steps:
- Incorrect merge in model weights or tokenizer change: revert to previous model artifact and start a validation PR.
- Quantization profile regression: rollback to previous quant-profile or re-run quantization with tighter calibration set.
- Serving runtime kernel/scheduling changes causing tokenization truncation: temporary rollback of runtime patch and file a follow-up kernel bug.
- Prompt-set drift (testing/benchmark gap): add failing prompts to canonical prompt set, update baseline, and notify teams to improve model or prompt engineering guidance.

Rollbacks and mitigations:
- Hot rollback to previous model version: follow model-rollout runbook (owner: model-onboarding). Use canary first (5% traffic) then expand if green.
- Quant-profile rollback: update model config to use prior profile id in the model catalog and redeploy.
- Routing policy fallback: update smart-router policy to prefer stable model variant for affected customers/regions.

Post-incident actions (within 5 working days):
- Postmortem: owner_team creates a blameless postmortem with timeline, RCA, and actions.
- Update eval harness: add or update prompt sets that surfaced the regression and ensure they are included in automated baseline runs.
- Quality guardrails: if regression was safety-related, add new safety checks and blocking alerts in the eval harness.
- Quantization profiles: add failing calibration samples to quant-profile training and add a pre-deploy check: quant-smoke-test >= baseline threshold.

Runbook snippets and CLI examples:
- Reproduce an eval run locally:
  git clone git@github.com:redwood/eval-harness.git && cd eval-harness
  make install-deps
  ./scripts/reproduce.sh --run-id <id> --model <model-id> --prompt-set critical-safety --out /tmp/repro

- Example JSON artifact to attach to ticket (flattened):
  {
    "run_id": "r-20261128-09a",
    "model_id": "open-llama-13b-redwood-v2",
    "delta": "3.4%",
    "suspected_cause": "quantization",
    "samples": "/tmp/triage-r-20261128-09a/samples.jsonl"
  }

SLOs and thresholds (operational guidance):
- Automated eval harness runs must complete nightly across canonical prompt-sets with 99% success.
- Triage lead acknowledges Sev-1 alerts within 15 minutes and assembles response within 60 minutes.
- Rollback or mitigation decision for Sev-1 must be executed within 3 hours of declaration.

Escalation matrix and communication:
1) Triage Lead -> Model Owner -> Release Engineer (if runtime) -> Head of Applied ML + Eng SRE.
2) Notify Customer Success for impacted customers and provide mitigation ETA.
3) Use incident channel #aml-regression and post a summary to status page if customer impact > 100 tenants.

Prevention and continuous improvement:
- Integrate quantization smoke tests into CI for every model-onboarding PR.
- Maintain a curated set of high-sensitivity prompt-sets used as gating checks for every rollout.
- Monthly cross-team reviews of the top 10 failing prompts and action items.
